title: Construction Fire Protection Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.150)
subtitle: For jobsite walks to check firefighting equipment, water supply, alarms and fire cutoffs.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Record each defect and the action taken; defective firefighting equipment must be replaced immediately under 1926.150(a)(4).
The manufacturer's instructions and site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Program, access and equipment condition
items: The site's fire protection program exists and covers the current phase of construction or demolition work
No materials, debris or vehicles block any extinguisher, hose rack, drum or standpipe outlet
Employer-provided firefighting equipment is in plain view or clearly marked where it is
Equipment is in operating condition; anything defective has been replaced, not left in place
Where the project warrants one, a trained and equipped fire brigade is in place

sections.title: Portable fire extinguishers
items: At least one extinguisher rated 2A or higher for each 3,000 sq ft, or major fraction, of the protected building area
No point in the protected area is more than 100 feet of travel from an extinguisher
One or more extinguishers rated 2A or higher on every floor
In a multistory building, at least one extinguisher sits adjacent to a stairway
A 10B-or-higher extinguisher within 50 feet wherever more than 5 gallons of flammable or combustible liquids or 5 pounds of flammable gas are in use (vehicle integral fuel tanks excluded)
Extinguishers and water drums exposed to freezing are protected from it
Each extinguisher is listed or approved by a nationally recognized testing laboratory
No carbon tetrachloride or other toxic vaporizing liquid extinguishers on site
Evidence that each portable extinguisher is inspected periodically and maintained per NFPA No. 10A-1970

sections.title: Water supply and hose lines
items: Once combustible materials have accumulated, water of sufficient volume, duration and pressure is available to run the firefighting equipment
Any drum used in place of a 2A extinguisher is a 55-gallon open drum of water with two fire pails
Hose is 1/2-inch, 100 feet or shorter, has a nozzle, delivers at least 5 gallons per minute and reaches at least 30 feet horizontally
Garden-type hose is on conventional racks or reels placed so a hose stream reaches all points in the area
Adapters or equivalent are on hand where hose connections don't fit local firefighting equipment
During demolition involving combustible materials, charged hose lines fed by hydrants, tank trucks with pumps or equivalent are available

sections.title: Sprinklers and standpipes
items: Where sprinklers are part of the facility, installation keeps pace with construction and is in service on completed stories where laws permit
During demolition or alterations, existing sprinklers remain in service as long as reasonable
Valves were checked at close of work today and show protection in service; only authorized persons operate them
Required or existing standpipes are brought up with the structure and ready for fire protection use
Fire department connection is outside the structure at street level and conspicuously marked
At least one standard hose outlet on each floor

sections.title: Alarms and fire cutoffs
items: A working means, such as a telephone system or siren, alerts employees on site and the fire department in an emergency
Alarm code and reporting instructions are posted where they are easy to see at phones and employee entrances
Fire doors with automatic closing devices are hung on openings once practicable
Fire cutoffs during alterations or demolition
Fire cutoffs remain in place until operations make removal necessary

references: 29 CFR 1926.150: Fire protection (Part 1926 Subpart F, Fire Protection and Prevention)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, text as of 2026-11-09
